chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said:

Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man who seized another man in order to kill him, and the man was fleeing from him, so another man came across him and restrained him for him until the first man came and killed him. So he (peace be upon him) said: The man who killed him would be killed (qisas), and the judgment upon the other one who restrained him is that he be thrown into prison forever until he dies in it, because he restrained him to the death.

key_terms.قَضَى: He judged / issued a legal ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling when one person restrains a victim for another who then kills him?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes a distinct category of liability for the 'restrainer' (al-mu'taqil), differentiating him from the direct killer by imposing life imprisonment rather than immediate execution. This precedent highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of assessing the causal link and intent behind each participant's action, where the restrainer’s confinement of the victim is viewed as a continuous act leading to death. It serves as a foundational text for understanding joint homicide (qatl bi-sharik) and the nuanced application of qisas in early Islamic legal theory.
